message.content: The last common ancestor of lions (family Felidae, order Carnivora) and zebras (family Equidae, order Perissodactyla) is a small, probably insect‑eating mammal that lived in the early Paleogene (about 60–70 million years ago). It belonged to the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which gave rise to many modern groups of placental mammals, including the carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates.
